messages:
maria: Quick runway check — hosted GPU reserved vs forecast for May spike. I just saw a +28% cloud bill delta on the invoices compared to forecast, and committed utilization is only ~62% on avg. Do we have a fresh supply/demand signal?

alex: I saw that too. My quick read: a lot of short-lived bulk embedding jobs in eu-west last week drove on-demand fallbacks. Committed pools didn't cover the burst pattern.

deepa: Can you paste the invoice line? is it preemptible/spot bounce or on-demand premium?

maria: finance-liaison pasted the line in thread: "Compute - g4dn/reserved vs on-demand - eu-west-1" — looks like on-demand invoicing for 48K tokens worth of runtime that should've hit reserved.

finance-liaison: Confirming: cloud charge shows ~72k USD for ephemeral GPU hours that were expected to be in reserved bucket. We flagged an instance mismatch tag that prevented auto-association to our reservations.

sam: Tag drift again? Which tag/time window?

finance-liaison: A subset 2024-04-28 -> 2024-05-04. Resource tags: project:redwood-hosted, environment:prod were missing on the job fleet that scaled up in eu-west.

alex: That explains it. The autoscaler spawns ephemeral nodes with label "ephemeral-burst" for bulk-embeds; our reservation rules require tag project:redwood-hosted to attach.

maria: OK, so two issues: forecast mismatch (we underpredicted burst), and reservation attachment gaps. We should re-run forecast with recent burst signal and patch tagging policy.

deepa: I'll run a quick run-rate forecast using the last 30 days plus an outlier window. Query I usually run: 

```
-- pseudo-SQL
SELECT date, SUM(gpu_hours) as hours
FROM hosted_usage
WHERE region = 'eu-west-1' AND workload IN ('embedding','generation')
GROUP BY date
ORDER BY date DESC
LIMIT 60;
```

I'll add 90th percentile smoothing and project to next 45 days.

sam: Also check prefix cache hit rates for embedding pipeline. If cache misses spiked, that explains extra compute.

alex: Good call. Cache logs show a big TTL expiry rollover on 2024-04-29 after we rotated cache namespace. That will increase GPU hours.

infra-bot: Alert: reservation-attachment-failures count=43 in eu-west-1 between 2024-04-28T03:00Z and 2024-05-04T22:00Z. Link: https://infra.redwood/alerts/RES-ATTACH-1763

maria: Action plan proposal:
1) deepa runs forecast & posts new projected reserved hours and 95th percentile runway (due EOD).
2) alex updates autoscaler to set project:redwood-hosted tag on ephemeral burst nodes + run a one-off reconciliation job to attach past unmatched instances (if cloud API allows).
3) sam investigates cache TTL rotation and if we can stagger rotations to avoid mass-misses.
4) finance-liaison to reconcile invoice line items once reconciliation runs.

alex: I can put a hotfix to autoscaler today (adds tag) and kick off reconcile script. If we can attach retroactively, that may reduce next invoice adjustment.

finance-liaison: Note: retro attachment doesn't always retro-bill reservations; cloud provider policy varies. I'll open a billing case but assume worst-case we absorb some cost. We'll need a buffer in reserved planning.

deepa: Posting provisional numbers: baseline reserved commit for eu-west = 3200 GPU-hours/day. Observed 14-day 95th = 4600 GPU-hours/day (with burst jobs). Projected next-30-days w/ conservative growth = ~4200 GPU-hours/day. That suggests shortfall of ~1000 GPU-hours/day if bursts repeat.

maria: Thanks. So immediate ask: can we borrow some committed capacity from other regions (failover) or re-route some low-SLA bulk embeds to cheaper zones?

alex: We have spare dedicated capacity in us-west for low-latency-tolerant jobs. Two levers: 1) traffic routing policy to send bulk-embeds to dedicated pool in us-west, 2) increase eu-west reservation by a small amount for the quarter. Routing change would require a quick feature flag and opt-in config in the job scheduler.

sam: Routing is feasible for embedding-only jobs — they tolerate extra latency. I'll prototype a region-based scheduler rule and a canary to 5% traffic.

maria: Cost comparison please: delta for increasing eu-west reservation vs routing 30% of bulk-embeds to us-west (incl egress cost). finance-liaison can you rough that out?

finance-liaison: Rough calc: adding 500 reserved GPU-hours/day in eu-west ~ 35k USD/month commit. Routing 30% of bulk embeds to us-west increases network/egress ~6k USD/month but saves ~22k USD on reservation delta (net ~ -16k vs adding full reservation). Need precise numbers after traffic profile.

alex: Given that, short-term routing + autoscaler tag fix + cache TTL mitigation reduces risk quickly. For Q next quarter we should plan a small reservation uplift and revisit after 6 weeks of telemetry.

maria: Agree. Assign owners: deepa (forecast + 95th analysis) -> EOD. alex (autoscaler tag + reconcile job) -> today. sam (cache TTL + region routing prototype) -> 48h. finance-liaison (billing case + cost calc) -> 48h. I'll coordinate follow-up and create a kanban ticket.

infra-bot: Task created: INFRA-1429 "eu-west reservation attach + routing prototype" assigned to alex, sam, deepa. Due: 2024-05-10.

maria: Thanks team. We'll re-open if the reconcile job can't attach past instances. If billing case returns with credit, we'll re-evaluate reservation uplift. :thumbsup:
